title: Op-Ed: Why the UN's Shipping Agency Must Adopt Its Climate Agreement
summary: The IMO's Net-Zero Framework (NZF) adoption remains stalled by political maneuvers, exposing the shipping industry's chronic resistance to meaningful decarbonization. While proposing a 30% emissions reduction by 2030, this framework is merely a proposal, offering no immediate accountability for current carbon intensity or excessive HFO usage. As global climate impacts escalate, this persistent inaction proves the industry's "green goals" remain detached from urgent, enforceable reality.
content:
That pressure resulted in postponement. As this next IMO meeting approaches, momentous midterm elections have changed the country’s political landscape. For now, it remains unclear whether the US will return to the IMO with the same tactics.

In any case, countries that supported the NZF when originally approved, but subsequently came under pressure to object to its adoption in October 2025, will now likely be reassessing their positions. They are likely wondering if they can again stand firm in support of the NZF in a new political landscape.

Adoption of the NZF “as is,” without further delay or distraction, is key to realizing the goals of the IMO’s GHG Strategy - decarbonization by 2050, with targets of a 30% reduction in absolute emissions by 2030 and 80% by 2040 - and to protecting our global climate.

Coming after years of negotiations, the Net-Zero Framework reflects the IMO’s own Comprehensive Impact Assessment and will deliver on its goals. The NZF brings together a multitude of interests and positions, is supported by a broad majority and is the shipping sector’s best shot at reducing climate-warming emissions.

Since October 2025, when IMO member states voted to adjourn the adoption session for one year, various alternative proposals to the NZF were introduced and discussed intensively. However, they were neither able to demonstrate a comparable reduction in emissions nor to gather sufficient support. The alternative proposals aimed at supplanting or distracting from the NZF have now fallen away, proving the NZF as the best course ahead.

In the ensuing period, the world has seen a year of increased climate impacts: floods, droughts, heatwaves, and wildfires. UNEP’s Limiting Overshoot Spotlight Report shows the consequences of global inaction: global warming is expected to cross 1.5°C, despite international obligations to protect the climate system from anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions.

There is no longer time for going in circles; every IMO member state must get behind the Net-Zero Framework and adopt it before the year ends.

Lukas Leppert is President of the Clean Shipping Coalition.
